title: lowfi-scorecard-and-debrief-samira-garcia
content:
Quick low-fi notes after loop with Samira Garcia (candidate) — written while things are still fresh. Intention: capture impressions, rough scorecard, follow-ups, and suggested next steps. Keep in users/ as scratch — will move to shared drive if we formalize.

Candidate summary:
- Role interviewed for: Senior Runtime Engineer (inference stack)
- Interview date: 2026-02-14 (loop of 4 interviews)
- Interviewers: Marcus (serving runtime), Priya (platform), me (runtime infra), Elena (SRE shadow)
- Background: 6+ years infra + ML systems, last at a startup building an embedded model-serving library; has experience shipping C++ runtime components and Python orchestration glue. Familiar with model caching patterns and production rollout infra.

High-level takeaways (bullet):
- Strong mental model of KV cache and prefix caching tradeoffs; gave concrete examples from previous product where caching improved p99 by ~40%
- Clear about batching vs latency SLOs and had useful heuristics (max batch size per GPU type + dynamic early-flush)
- Limited exposure to low-level CUDA/kernel tuning — has people who did that at prior company; she wrote shim layers and profiling dashboards but didn't author custom kernels
- Good product sense: asked about UX for rollout policies and fallback model variants, suggested sensible defaults
- Communication felt pragmatic and collaborative — good candidate for cross-team pairing

Whiteboard / design exercise (30m):
Task: design a shared KV cache and multi-tenant batching layer for low-latency chat workloads across model family variants.
- Proposed architecture: per-tenant logical cache with global eviction policy + LRU-ish per-key freshness windows; batching router that prioritizes small latency-critical requests (short-circuit) and opportunistic batching for background requests
- Pros: addresses hot-key pressure and tenant isolation, acknowledged memory fragmentation concerns
- Missing / weak: specifics on memory accounting across quantized model variants (32-bit v 8-bit) and how to handle heterogenous GPU memory pools; no concrete algorithm for admission control under bursty load (had ideas but not a polished controller)

Coding/debugging session (45m):
- Given a reproduced p99 regression triggered by a new quantization path; asked to triage logs and suggest mitigation
- Strength: quickly isolated likely causes to two places — KV cache poisoning by stale keys and a change to compilation flags that changed kernel launch shapes
- Showed solid approach to narrowing repro (local trace captures, synthetic workload)
- Weakness: less comfortable with reading raw CUDA profiler timeline; would defer to infra engineer for low-level GPU root cause

Behavior / culture fit:
- Strong ownership examples: led an initiative to rewrite a runtime component to reduce tail latency; drove rollout and observed metrics post-deploy
- Curious about cross-team collaboration; asked good questions about on-call expectations and incident postmortem culture

Rough scorecard (0-10 scale)
- Core systems design: 7
- Production debugging & triage: 7
- Low-level performance (kernels/CUDA): 5
- Distributed systems & scaling: 6.5
- Communication / collaboration: 8
- Ownership & product sense: 8
- Overall (average, weighted toward production readiness): 7.1

Concerns and risk areas (short):
- Not a kernel author — would need pairing or mentorship for CUDA-level work if role requires it
- Limited experience with multi-region routing and automated fallback policies at extreme scale (100k QPS)
- Less depth on memory/quantization interplay across model variants (we need someone who can recommend quantization knobs for performance vs quality tradeoffs)

Strengths and value adds:
- Solid pragmatic engineer for production inference pipelines — good for owning batching, caching, routing components
- Product-minded: will likely improve developer-facing defaults and rollout UX
- Fast at debugging high-level regressions and orchestrating mitigation plans (cache invalidation, temporary config rollbacks)

Suggested next steps (practical):
- Recommend 1) follow-up deep dive focused on "kernel and quantization tradeoffs" with a member of the applied-ml team (90 min). Goal: probe depth on quantization experience and whether candidate can drive quantization policy recommendations.
- 2) take-home micro-assignment (48–72h): implement a simple in-memory LRU cache with metrics + a short write-up describing how to adapt it for multi-GPU quantized model variants (we're not evaluating kernel code, more the thought process).
- 3) references: two technical refs (one manager, one peer) — ask specifically about CUDA/kernel ownership and scale runbooks.

Hiring recommendation (draft):
- Stage: advance to deep-technical follow-up (not immediate hire).
- Level: Senior (IC3) seems appropriate; could stretch to Senior+ if the deep dive shows kernel/quantization competence.
- Compensation band suggestion (prelim): US-market Senior runtime band — $200k-$240k base + equity; flexible depending on level and negotiation.

Notes for interview packet (if we progress):
- Add a link to prior open-source repos where candidate contributed runtime pieces (asked, said private at last company but has a public helper lib)
- Include an explicit question set around quantization decisions and memory accounting for the follow-up interview

Open questions I want answered in follow-up:
- Has she designed or reviewed custom CUDA kernels or only integrated them? If only integrated, what did she own end-to-end when a kernel change regressed production?
- Exact scale numbers she shipped for (QPS, concurrent sessions, memory footprint per model variant)
- Comfort level with on-call rotation that includes direct-level inferencing incidents (doable or needs senior on-call backup?)

Action items (this doc is my todo):
- Send Samira quick thank-you + scheduling options for deep dive (Marcus to lead the kernel/quantization deep dive) — target week of 2026-02-23
- Draft take-home assignment prompt (I will sketch, Marcus to review)
- Add a short blurb for recruiting packet summarizing recommendation and flags

Last quick impressions (free-form):
- Likely strong hire for a team focused on inference orchestration and developer experience; borderline if the role needs heavy kernel engineering immediately. If we have Senior+ kernel expert on team to pair with, she would be an excellent contributor.
- Candidate proactivity: good questions about observability and rollback. Seems product-aware, low ego.

-- Noah
